top.title: F1 makes final call on Qatar and Abu Dhabi amid Middle East situation
top.description: Formula 1 has confirmed that end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as scheduled. The final two rounds of the 2026 season in Qatar (29 November) and Abu Dhabi (6 December) had been shrouded in uncertainty due to the conflict in the Middle East . Races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia earlier this season were cancelled , though Bahrain did fulfil its event with a one-off race in Malaysia in October. F1 did have the historic Imola circuit as a back-up contingency plan for 6 December, with preliminary grandstand work underway in and around the track site in the Emilia Romagna region of Italy. However, given logistical and freight plans, The Independent understands that F1 has now told Imola to stand down. Qatar and Abu Dhabi will conclude the campaign as planned as part of one final triple-header, starting in Las Vegas on 21 November. An F1 spokesperson added: “We are very grateful for the support and collaboration with the promoter and government in Imola and the region. If the situation develops negatively in the coming weeks before the events in the Middle East we will not hesitate to do the right thing and the safety of everyone will always be the priority.” F1 added that all 11 teams are supportive of concluding the season as planned. The final round of the MotoGP season took place in Qatar – at the same circuit in Lusail, just outside Doha – over the weekend without a hitch, though Yamaha did withdraw from the event pre-race. Nineteen riders also penned a letter expressing their wish not to race in Qatar, but both races were held as planned. Previous UK travel guidance during the height of the US/Israel-Iran conflict this year advised against “all but essential” travel to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However, that has since been lifted, with tension in the region cooling in recent weeks. That being said, the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) does state that the “broader security context” in the Middle East “carries a risk of sudden escalation, potential flight cancellations and airspace disruptions.” Both F1 chief Stefano Domenicali and FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem have insisted in recent weeks that the Middle Eastern races will take place as planned, barring any sudden re-escalation of hostilities in the region. Moto GP finished their season in Qatar on Sunday (Reuters) Mercedes boss Toto Wolff, whose team clinched the constructors’ championship in Brazil last weekend, a week after Kimi Antonelli won the drivers’ title, has backed the sport to make the right call. top.title: “Doesn’t Hurt That You Have $50M+”: Kyle Whittingham Shifts Attention to Oregon’s Massive Recruiting Budget Ahead of Ducks Clash
top.description: Michigan football head coach Kyle Whittingham speaks as he is being introduced on the floor during the first half between Michigan and USC at Crisler Center © Imagn Michigan football is at a crossroads as it aims to rescue its college football season, and the pressure is on Kyle Whittingham. The Wolverines’ head coach made the decision to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck after an unsatisfactory run of performances, but he still needs to win games to keep his own job secure. Ahead of the game against the Oregon Ducks, who are themselves turning a corner after some tough results, Whittingham shifted attention to Oregon’s massive recruiting budget, highlighting the difference between the two sides. “He really does a great job recruiting and it doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million dollars at your disposal to, in essence outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that’s not his fault,” Whittingham said about head coach Dan Lanning to reporters, via Inside Michigan . He further said that he meant it as a credit to the program and its desire to focus on young athletes in the NIL era. “That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much,” he went on. Kyle Whittingham Explained Why He Fired Jason Beck After a tough defeat to Michigan State, offensive coordinator Jason Beck received his marching orders from Kyle Whittingham, and he addressed the decision to media personnel. “Well, watching the film really was the deciding factor, and I had the intention of waiting until after the season, as I mentioned,” Whittingham said to reporters, as reported by Wolverines Wire . He further revealed when it became completely clear to him that a change was needed. “But when I turned the film on and really dove into it, it just became apparent to me that you need to make the change now. And there’s just too much regression in the offense in that particular game. And that’s what led to the decision.” Whittingham also confirmed no other person was involved in making the decision but himself. The decision will be put to the test as the Wolverines play the Oregon Ducks on Saturday. top.title: Greyson Fuller's 1,000-yard season is only a first step to become South's next great QB
top.description: EAST STROUDSBURG – Is Greyson Fuller the next great East Stroudsburg South quarterback? The jury is still out, but the junior signal-caller took the first step towards earning that distinction. Fuller, who completed his first season as the full-time starter for the Cavaliers after stepping up as a sophomore in 2025, became the 17 th South QB to throw for at least 1,000 yards in a single season, finishing the 2026 campaign with 1,767 yards. He nearly reached this milestone last season after filling in for an injured Ivan Laubach, but now the milestone is officially his. “It feels great,” Fuller said about the accomplishment. “I grew up looking at the banner hanging in the gym of all the 1,000-yard guys, and it’s going to be awesome seeing my name up there.” Going to the 'ship: East football avenges Bucket Game loss, beats PV to advance to 5A district title game South head coach Matt Walters has consistently commended Fuller’s development from his sophomore year to his junior year, and he’s proud of how he reached the milestone. As great as the milestone is, however, it’s only a first step on the path to be among the program greats. Granted, Fuller’s 1,767 yards rank him seventh all-time in program history for single-season passing yards, and 15 th all-time amongst all Pocono quarterbacks. But here are the fellow Cavaliers ahead of him: Jake Cirillo, who threw for 1,000 yards all four years of high school before going to play for East Stroudsburg University Ivan Laubach, a 2,000-yard passer who led South to a district championship. Bobby McClosky, an EPC North MVP, and a First Team All-State Selection And Rob Moyer, the area’s all-time leader in single-season passing yards, and the only player in Pocono history to pass for 2,000 yards twice Even some of the names behind Fuller who lack in numbers make up for the difference in accolades. ESU head coach Jimmy Terwilliger was the first East Stroudsburg (before the split) quarterback to have multiple 1,000-yard seasons, and he did that with a coach who ran the option in the legend Ed Christian. Oh yeah, and he later earned the honor of the best player in Division II football. And there’s also Will Fish, who joined the 1,000-yard club in 2019 and nearly threw for 2,000 his junior year and went on to play at Lycoming College. Fish is now on staff at South, where he watched Fuller throw for 303 passing yards and five touchdowns against Pocono Mountain West. “Coach Fish talked to me on the sidelines midgame and asked me how many touchdowns I was at,” Fuller said. “He then said, ‘All right, my record is six touchdowns. top.title: Managerial 'inconsistency' hurting Ghana - Hughton
top.description: Kim Bjorkegren (right) is in interim charge of Ghana after Carlos Queiroz left the Black Stars by mutual consent [Getty Images] As Ghana prepare for two make-or-break 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifiers with women's coach Kim Bjorkegren in temporary charge, former boss Chris Hughton has called for greater consistency in the Black Stars dugout. The West Africans face Somalia in back-to-back fixtures over the next week, having lost their first two games in Group C against Ivory Coast and The Gambia last month. Those defeats resulted in the departure of Carlos Queiroz, whose brief period in the hot seat was characterised by uncertainty. The Portuguese's exit means Swede Bjorkegren, who has been in charge of the Black Queens since January 2025, has now been asked to lead the men's team against Somalia. "When you have inconsistency in the amount of time when a manager is staying, it's never good," Hughton told BBC Sport Africa. "You want that consistency in the players [and] the players want that consistency in what they see in the manager." Queiroz, who had two spells as Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant at Manchester United, was initially appointed in April and led Ghana to the last 32 of the Fifa World Cup, holding England to a goalless draw in the group stage, before announcing his own departure shortly after the team were eliminated 1-0 by Colombia in the last 32. However, the 73-year-old was reappointed in early September, with the Ghana Football Association (GFA) praising his "extensive international experience" gained during time in charge of South Africa, Egypt, Portugal, Iran, Colombia, Qatar and Oman. But Queiroz's return lasted less than a month following a 2-0 defeat by the Ivorians in Bouake and a 4-2 humbling against the Gambians in front of home fans in Accra. "What I saw in the World Cup is that they represented the country very well, particularly the England game," said Hughton. "And although it was very much a defensive outfit, there were opportunities to score." Hughton, however, admits that regular sackings can create an "attitude" within a squad, with players knowing that "if he (the coach) doesn't do well then he won't be there". top.title: Vikings vs. Packers odds: Vikings underdogs heading into Lambeau
top.description: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 09: Christian Benford #47 of the Buffalo Bills breaks up a pass intended for Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at U.S. Bank Stadium on November 09, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don’t like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday’s game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that’s just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don’t do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

top.title: FIA boss looks to ‘end age limits’ for office holders – six months after ditching term limits
top.description: Mohammed Ben Sulayem is reportedly looking to end age limits for FIA office holders – just six months after the FIA president ditched term limits for those in leadership posts. Emirati executive Ben Sulayem, 64, has been FIA president since December 2021 and was re-elected last year after other candidates were prevented from standing, due to quirks in the FIA statutes which meant the only prospective vice-president in one region was already aligned with Ben Sulayem. Currently, FIA statutes rule out anyone over the age of 75 from standing for a presidential term. This rule was implemented in 2024 to “modernise the governance of the FIA and ensure that candidates for the presidency are more aligned with current leadership practices.” Yet just six months after Ben Sulayem ended term limits for those in leadership posts, the BBC reports that Ben Sulayem wants to discontinue the age-limit rule and put forward a proposal detailing as such to the FIA’s General Assembly in Shanghai next month. An FIA spokesperson told The Independent: “An age limit excludes candidates solely on the basis of their date of birth, regardless of their experience, expertise, or ability to contribute. Ultimately, the competent FIA bodies will retain full authority to elect the officeholders they deem appropriate.” “The proposal to remove age limits for FIA officeholders is one of the proposed amendments to the FIA Statutes to be put to the General Assembly in Shanghai in December. It was approved by the World Councils for submission in line with the process set out in the FIA Statutes, and will only take effect if the General Assembly votes in favour.” Ben Sulayem had originally introduced an upper age limit of 70 in 2023, in a move widely seen to prevent Motorsport UK boss David Richards from running. Ben Sulayem, who is a regular in parc ferme and on the podium after F1 races, has overseen controversial moments in his near-five years in charge. Ben Sulayem has clashed with Max Verstappen in the past (Getty) His first term saw Ben Sulayem clash with Lewis Hamilton over the Brit’s desire to wear jewellery in the cockpit, while he also angered drivers, including four-time world champion Max Verstappen, for issuing fines for swearing. Last April, Robert Reid resigned as deputy president for sport, accusing the governing body of a "breakdown in governance standards." top.title: Former Royals catcher and manager Bob Boone dies at age 78
top.description: BOSTON, MA - MAY 22: Bob Boone #8 of the Kansas City Royals takes a swing during a baseball game against the Boston Red Sox on May 22, 1989 at Fenway Park in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher who spent two seasons as a player with the Kansas City Royals before managing the club for parts of three seasons, has died at the age of 78, according to a social media post from his family . The son of All-Star infielder Ray Boone, and the father of All-Star infielders Bret and Aaron Boone, the Boones were the first family to have three generations of MLB players. RIP Bob Boone, the great Gold Glove, All Star and World Series champion catcher, who passes away at 78. Condolences to wife Sue and sons Aaron and Bret Boone. What a marvelous man and privilege and honor to know. — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) November 10, 2026 Bob Boone was one of the most accomplished defensive catchers of his generation, winning seven Gold Glove Awards over a 19-year playing career. He was originally drafted by the Philadelphia Phillies after a standout career at Stanford. He he finished third in Rookie of the Year voting and was a three-time All-Star with the Phillies. He faced the Royals in the 1980 World Series as a catcher for the Phillies, hitting .412 (7-for-17) in the series for his only championship. He moved onto the Angels in 1982, helping them win the division in their first year, earning MVP votes, and winning a Gold Glove. He was an All-Star the next year, and over seven years in Anaheim, he set the club record for most games behind the plate. He left Anaheim and signed with the Royals in 1989 at the age of 41. He appeared in 131 games and hit .274/.351/.323, winning his seventh Gold Glove and finishing with 2.4 rWAR. After 40 games in 1990, he retired. After the 1994 season was cancelled during the work stoppage, the Royals hired Bob Boone as manager to replace Hal McRae and usher in a new youth movement. Despite trading away stars like David Cone and Brian McRae, the Royals were in the hunt for the new “Wild Card” spot for most of the season, until a poor September caused them to fall under .500 at 70-74. Boone was a very cerebral manager, but would frequently clash with the media. He was criticized for constantly changing the lineup, and for employing “Boonieball,” as then-Kansas City Star columnist Jeffrey Flanagan would call his style of play. Boone finished just 75-86 in 1996, and was fired at the 1997 All-Star break after a 36-46 start, replaced by Tony Muser. Boone would later manage the Cincinnati Reds from 2001-2003, although he never managed them to a winning season. He joined the Washington Nationals front office in 2005 and served the team until he retired in 2021.

top.title: USMNT could lose head coach just months after signing extension
top.description: Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - United States Press Conference - Los Angeles Stadium, Inglewood, California, U.S. - June 11, 2026 U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino during the press conference REUTERS/Daniel Cole Manchester United have gotten off to the worst start in their Premier League history, and it looks like Michael Carrick is about to pay the price. The club is reportedly ready to fire its manager, with United sitting in the relegation zone after just one win in 10 league games. And United’s top choice to replace him could come as a big blow to American soccer fans. U.S. men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly the favorite for the job, less than four months after signing a contract extension with U.S. Soccer. Pochettino and the USMNT Pochettino took over the USMNT in 2024 with the goal of leading the team on a deep run in the World Cup on home soil. Instead, the U.S. was eliminated in the Round of 16 by Belgium in a blowout loss. That run also came with its share of controversy. Pochettino later admitted it was a “mistake” after FIFA overturned a suspension to Folarin Balogun ahead of the Belgium match, a decision that came after President Donald Trump said he had contacted FIFA president Gianni Infantino about it. He also didn’t mince words about Christian Pulisic’s struggles. Still, U.S. Soccer stood by Pochettino after the tournament, and in August, it announced that he had signed a new deal that runs through the 2030 World Cup. Manchester United’s Interest According to ESPN’s Mark Ogden and Rob Dawson , United’s leadership, including co-chairman Joel Glazer and minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, has been assessing Carrick’s future. Sources told ESPN that there is “now acceptance that performances and results demand a change of manager.” Carrick took over as interim manager in January and led United to Champions League qualification, earning a two-year contract this summer. But the club has won just one of four games since giving him time to turn things around last month, leaving United one point off the bottom of the table. Pochettino, who has interviewed for the United job three times before, is regarded as having “the Premier League experience and personality needed to drag United out of danger,” per the report. The former Tottenham, Chelsea, and PSG manager also reportedly has a $10 million escape clause in his U.S. Soccer contract, which United would have to pay. Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann, and Kieran McKenna are also reportedly among the candidates. United’s next match is against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22. nigeria.title: Meet only two countries to have won both men’s, women’s U-20 World Cups
nigeria.description: Germany and Spain are the only two countries to have won both the FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup and the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup. The two European nations have achieved the feat by winning titles in both competitions, which showcase some of the world’s best emerging football talents. Germany became the first to accomplish the double, with its men’s team, then competing as West Germany, winning the U-20 World Cup in 1981. The country’s women’s team subsequently claimed the U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2004, 2010 and 2014, taking its tally to three titles in the competition. Spain also joined the exclusive list after winning the men’s U-20 World Cup in 1999, when the tournament was hosted by Nigeria. The Spanish men’s team defeated Japan 4-0 in the final in Lagos to secure its first title. More than two decades later, Spain’s women’s team won its maiden U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2022, defeating Japan 3-1 in the final in Costa Rica. Spain added a second women’s title in 2026, further strengthening its record across both competitions. The achievement places Germany and Spain in a select group of countries that have conquered both sides of FIFA’s U-20 World Cup competitions. nigeria.title: Kompany returns to Bayern’s training ground for first time since collapse
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club’s training ground on Tuesday for the first time since collapsing last month, beginning a gradual return to work ahead of the Bundesliga match against Cologne on November 20. The 40-year-old was at Bayern’s Säbener Straße complex shortly after 10am, according to German media reports. He worked from his office, spoke with assistant coach Floribert Ngalula and sporting director Christoph Freund, and watched injured players complete a recovery session. His return to the training ground does not mean he has resumed all his duties, as he is expected back in the dugout after the international break. Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team. He was hospitalised and diagnosed with meningeal irritation, an inflammation affecting the tissue around the brain or spinal cord. He was later discharged to recover at home. Assistant Aaron Danks took charge during Kompany’s absence, overseeing four wins and a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund. Bayern beat Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atlético Madrid and Mainz. Danks said the club had instructed him to keep football discussions away from Kompany while he recovered. “I have clear instructions from Max [Eberl] and Christoph [Freund] not to engage in discussions, first of all, and to keep Vince focused on nothing other than his health and spending time with his family,” he said. “We want him to rest and recover properly so that, when he returns, he is fully fit and can help us in the best possible way. We are being very strict here and keeping football completely out of it.” Kompany’s father, Pierre, had previously described his son’s demanding work routine in an interview with Bild. “He works 18 hours a day most days and, on a typical day, barely sees his children,” he said, adding that Kompany was often at the training ground early and left late. Bayern are scheduled to host Cologne on November 20, when Kompany is expected to return to the touchline. nigeria.title: 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway pileup
nigeria.description: Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU. Crashes in thick fog snared dozens of vehicles heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas. An estimated 50 cars and trucks were involved in the accident near the city of Yambol, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency, as government officials rushed to the scene. Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles. “The toll at this point is 11 dead and 48 injured,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters. Radev was meeting EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, who is on a visit to Bulgaria, but the prime minister cancelled his official events scheduled for later Tuesday. The injured were transported to hospitals in nearby cities. The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams. Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures. Victims blame the Balkan nation’s high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system. Stricter penalties Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed “deepest condolences” to the victims and their families in a post on X. European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was “deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning”. A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 — down five percent from the previous year and 27 percent lower than in 2019. The EU in 2019 introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 percent by 2030. A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains “one of the world’s safest regions for road travel”, the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target. The report said that just five of the EU’s 27 countries — including Bulgaria — were on track to meet the target. However, “despite their progress since 2019, Bulgaria and Romania, alongside Croatia, continue to have the highest fatality rates in the EU when measuring deaths per million inhabitants”, the report said. In 2023, Bulgaria’s parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs. The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record. Bulgaria’s busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts. But Bulgaria’s status as the EU’s poorest member state also plays a role, with around half of the cars registered more than 20 years old. Vanguard News The post 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway

nigeria.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has disclosed that less than 36 per cent of Nigerians have access to improved toilet facilities, raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges and the associated public health risks. The Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, disclosed this on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day. Lawal, who was represented by the Director of Pollution Control and Environmental Health, Mrs Omotunde Adeola, said many public places, including markets, motor parks, schools and communities, still lacked adequate and functional toilet facilities. He warned that the situation was contributing to open defecation, contamination of food and water sources, and the spread of sanitation-related diseases such as cholera and typhoid. According to him, inadequate sanitation poses serious threats to public health, environmental safety and human dignity. The minister said women, girls, children, older persons and persons living with disabilities were particularly affected by the shortage of appropriate sanitation facilities. He stressed that no child should miss school because of inadequate toilet facilities, while no woman or girl should be forced to compromise her safety and dignity because of the absence of suitable toilets. Providing a global perspective, Lawal said about 4.5 billion people worldwide still lacked safely managed sanitation, while 892 million continued to practise open defecation. He said the figures underscored the need to accelerate efforts towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those relating to clean water and sanitation, gender equality, good health and sustainable communities by 2030. Government interventions On efforts to address the challenge, the minister said the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with relevant ministries, state governments and development partners, was implementing programmes to improve sanitation and promote safe excreta disposal nationwide. Other interventions, he said, included integrating sanitation into climate adaptation and circular economy initiatives, as well as partnering with private sector operators to provide environmentally friendly sanitation facilities. nigeria.title: Troops rescue three kidnap victims, kill two terrorists in Adamawa
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK) have rescued three kidnapped civilians and killed two terrorists in separate operations in Adamawa State. The troops also recovered two AK-47 rifles, ammunition, locally fabricated explosive devices, stolen vehicles and farm produce belonging to residents who narrowly escaped abduction. The Acting Media Information Officer of OPHK, Capt. Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday. He said the three victims were rescued by troops deployed in Mubi following a distress call from farmers around Dutse-Uku in Mubi South Local Government Area. According to him, suspected kidnappers abducted a farmer, identified as Happiness Dama Dauda, on November 9 while she was working on her farm and also stole her motorcycle. Goni said the troops, working with local hunters, mobilised to the area and mounted pressure on the kidnappers, forcing them to abandon their victim and flee. He added that a sustained pursuit led to the rescue of two other residents suspected to have been abducted earlier, bringing the number of rescued victims to three. The troops also recovered a motorcycle, a tricycle conveying 15 bags of beans and a Hi-Jet pickup carrying 13 bags of groundnuts belonging to other farmers who narrowly escaped abduction. Goni said the respective village heads identified the recovered items, which were subsequently handed over to their owners. Two terrorists killed in Gombi In a separate operation on November 8, troops deployed at Zangula Kilba Junction in Gombi Local Government Area foiled an attempted attack by suspected Boko Haram/Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists. Two terrorists were killed during the encounter, while others fled following what the military described as the troops’ superior combat readiness and tactical resilience. Items recovered from the fleeing insurgents included two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 115 rounds of ammunition, three belts of empty ammunition links and two cases of locally fabricated explosive devices. Other recovered items included a pair of desert boots, a backpack, an Android phone, a wristwatch and N15,000. Goni said troops had commenced exploitation operations to track down the fleeing terrorists and prevent them from regrouping. He added that troops were maintaining aggressive patrols and surveillance across the affected areas to prevent further attacks and reassure residents of their safety. The military urged residents to provide timely and credible intelligence to security agencies, stressing that collaboration between troops and local communities remained critical to tackling terrorism and other security threats. Operation Hadin Kai reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining operational pressure on terrorists and their collaborators to deny them the freedom to threaten the security and livelihoods of residents across the North-East. nigeria.description: By Chioma Okoye Fifteen nursing students of Madonna University, Nigeria, have appealed to the university management to reverse their expulsion and suspension over a controversial TikTok video recorded during their community posting, pleading for another opportunity to complete their studies. They also appreciated the university management for engaging with their parents and guardians and allowing them to present their concerns. nigeria.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says it will be immensely difficult for opposition parties to unseat President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. Wike said this in Abuja on Tuesday, after inspecting some ongoing projects within the federal capital territory. He cited what he described as Tinubu’s undeniable and rich report card of infrastructure development across the country. The minister said that the volume and pace of visible achievements delivered under Tinubu’s administration left very little room for political detractors to challenge the ruling party’s record. “You can see clearly that it will be difficult to unseat the president today because the report card is obvious in terms of what he has done. “Like I told you, this is our campaign. People ask what we are going to campaign with, but we have so many visible achievements all around us. “There is no way residents of Abuja will see the kind of infrastructure we have provided and say they are not happy with the achievements of Mr President. It is second to none,” he said. Highlighting the rapid speed of execution on several key projects in the territory, Wike referenced the rapid transformation of the Southern Parkway project, which was flagged during the celebration of Tinubu’s third year in office. “Within six to seven months, you can see what has been achieved. “It is unimaginable, and that is why we are very happy,” Wike said. nigeria.title: Gombe records 98 road crash deaths, 1,345 injuries in nine months — FRSC
nigeria.description: By Ben Ngwakwe GOMBE — The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) has disclosed that 98 persons were killed while 1,345 others sustained injuries in road traffic crashes recorded across Gombe State between January and September 2026. The FRSC Sector Commander in the state, Commander Samson Kaura, disclosed this on Tuesday in Gombe while addressing members of the Gombe State Council of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) during the commemoration of the 2026 World Day of Remembrance for Road Traffic Victims. Kaura said the command recorded 1,345 road traffic incidents during the nine-month period, adding that fatalities increased by six per cent compared with the corresponding period. He identified excessive speeding and reckless driving as major causes of road crashes and fatalities, warning that irresponsible road use continued to pose a serious threat to motorists and other road users. According to him, the annual World Day of Remembrance provides an opportunity to honour those who have lost their lives or sustained serious injuries in road crashes, while drawing attention to the need for stronger legal responses to traffic offences resulting in deaths and injuries. He said the commemoration also seeks to promote better support for crash victims and their families, as well as evidence-based interventions to prevent and ultimately eliminate road traffic deaths and injuries. The sector commander expressed concern that the fatalities recorded in the first nine months of 2026 had surpassed the figure for the whole of 2025. He said the command recorded 1,614 road traffic incidents in 2025, resulting in 92 deaths and 926 injuries. Kaura described the 2026 World Day of Remembrance as a campaign aimed at translating remembrance into concrete action, stressing the need for collective responsibility in addressing road traffic crashes. In his response, the Vice Chairman of the Gombe State NUJ Council, Emmanuel Akila, who represented the state chairman, Faruk Muazu Gombe, pledged the union’s continued cooperation with the FRSC in promoting road safety and development. Akila, however, urged the FRSC to strengthen collaboration with the union to identify and curb the activities of fake journalists in the state. He called on the corps to insist on proper identification of journalists during official engagements and other road-related activities to prevent impersonation and protect the integrity of the journalism profession. The NUJ vice chairman also urged the FRSC to intensify enforcement against vehicle overloading, describing the practice as one of the factors contributing to fatalities in road crashes. He stressed the need for sustained public enlightenment, effective enforcement of traffic regulations and stronger collaboration among relevant stakeholders to reduce road crashes and safeguard lives on the highways. nigeria.title: Ologe highlights growing importance of risk leadership in digital business
nigeria.description: Mojisola Ologe, an Associate Chartered Risk Manager, has highlighted the growing importance of risk management in strengthening corporate governance, business performance and operational resilience amid increasing digitalisation. Ologe, who received the professional designation from the Chartered Risk Management Institute of Nigeria (CRMI) on October 15, 2026, said effective risk management was becoming increasingly important as organisations expanded their reliance on technology and digital services. She noted that decisions involving access to information systems, introduction of new services, third-party dependencies and business recovery arrangements could have direct implications for customers, regulatory compliance and organisational credibility. Her professional experience spans consulting, banking and digital payments, including roles at Phillips Consulting and Sterling Bank, where she worked across technology assurance, information technology risk and control, business continuity and compliance oversight. The experience, according to her, has reinforced the need to translate identified operational and technological weaknesses into practical business implications and corrective actions. Ologe currently serves as Chief Risk and Compliance Officer at Hydrogen Payment Services Limited, where her responsibilities cover enterprise risk management, regulatory compliance, cybersecurity governance and operational resilience. In the digital payments sector, these areas are closely interconnected, as disruptions to technology systems can quickly affect customer services, expose businesses to financial losses and create regulatory challenges. Effective risk management, therefore, goes beyond identifying potential threats to understanding business operations, assessing critical dependencies and ensuring that management takes timely corrective action. Clear accountability, appropriate internal controls and effective escalation mechanisms are also essential to helping organisations address vulnerabilities while pursuing their business objectives. Ologe’s professional recognition by CRMI underscores the importance of continuous professional development in the risk management sector, particularly as emerging technologies and changing business conditions create new operational and regulatory challenges. Risk professionals, increasingly, are expected to contribute beyond compliance monitoring by providing insights that inform corporate strategy, investment decisions and everyday business operations. Their role, the profile noted, is to help organisations pursue growth while maintaining a clear understanding of potential exposures and strengthening their capacity to withstand disruptions. nigeria.title: US reps schedule fresh hearing on ‘Christian persecution’ in Nigeria
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The United States House of Representatives is set to hold a congressional hearing on Nigeria’s efforts to protect Christians and tackle insecurity in the Middle Belt, with Republican lawmaker Chris Smith leading the session on Thursday, November 12. According to a statement issued by Smith’s office on Monday, the session is titled ‘One Year Later: Assessing Nigeria’s Efforts to Protect Christians and Secure the Middle Belt’, with hearing scheduled for 11am at the Rayburn House Office Building in Washington, DC. It partly reads, “Congressional hearing that assesses the current state of religious violence perpetrated by radical Islamists, such as Boko Haram and Fulani terrorists, against Christians in Nigeria; the Nigerian government’s efforts to curb the persecution and punish those responsible for committing atrocities against Christian and non-radical Muslim communities; and the steps the United States can take to ensure that Nigerian officials are addressing and preventing the systemic violence against Christians and non-radical Muslims by Islamist extremists.” The first panel will feature Frank Garcia, Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs, and Riley Barnes, Assistant Secretary of State for Democracy, Human Rights and Labour. The second panel will include Nina Shea, senior fellow and director of the Centre for Religious Freedom at the Hudson Institute; Ryan Brown, chief executive officer of Open Doors US; and Oge Onubogu, director and senior fellow of the Africa Programme at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies. nigeria.title: Carrick set to be sacked by Man Utd: reports
nigeria.description: Michael Carrick is set to be sacked by Manchester United after his side’s dismal start to the season, according to reports on Tuesday. United’s hierarchy have been conducting an internal review of the club’s miserable form and it is believed that Carrick will shortly be relieved of his duties. United are in the midst of their worst opening to a campaign in 40 years, leaving them languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after an eight-match winless run. Although it is said that no final decision has been made, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are reportedly leaning towards dismissing Carrick. United owners the Glazer family and influential shareholder Jim Ratcliffe would then decide whether to act on that recommendation. Carrick was seen arriving at United’s Carrington training base on Tuesday, but it appears to be only a matter of time before his turbulent reign comes to an end. The 45-year-old, hired on a permanent basis in the close season after a successful interim spell last term, had been granted a stay of execution after he was widely expected to be axed in late October following a 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth. United’s surprise decision to let Carrick limp on failed to produce a significant improvement in performances, particularly defensively. They were beaten 2-0 at Chelsea, then scrambled a last-gasp 3-2 win against Roma in the Champions League after falling two goals down. It looked certain that former United midfielder Carrick would be on the way out when his team twice trailed by two goals against Aston Villa on Sunday. When United scored twice in stoppage-time to rescue an improbable 4-4 draw, it was interpreted as a positive sign for Carrick as the players were still fighting for him. But United’s powerbrokers look set to make yet another managerial change in a bid to avoid being dragged into an embarrassing relegation battle. USA boss Mauricio Pochettino, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe, ex-Chelsea chief Antonio Conte and former Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the United job. United have the rest of the two-week international break to secure a replacement for Carrick before returning to action at bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22. business.title: Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Amundi Boosts Strategy (MSTR) Stake 44% to $291 Million as Shares Slide Amundi, Europe’s largest asset manager, raised its stake in Strategy (MSTR) by about 44% in the third quarter, a Form 13F filed Nov. 6 shows, lifting the position to 1,903,725 shares worth $291.4 million at Sept. 30 prices. That is up 579,672 shares from the 1,324,053 Amundi reported at June 30, when the same holding was valued at about $115.1 million. The Paris-based firm managed €2.579 trillion in assets at the end of September, up 11% year over year, and described itself as Europe’s leading asset manager. The filing lands as MSTR has given back much of its third-quarter run. Strategy shares closed at $153.09 on Sept. 30 and near $126 on Monday, an 18% drop that would put Amundi’s disclosed stake near $239 million at the latest close, Yahoo Finance data show. A 13F is a snapshot, not a trading diary. Amundi filed a combination report that folds in 17 other managers across its group, so the Strategy line can include client, fund and discretionary positions rather than a single proprietary bet, and the firm may have changed the holding since Sept. 30. Strategy keeps buying while the stock slides Strategy itself kept stacking. The company bought another 1,036 bitcoin last week for $81.9 million at an average of $79,012, a Monday 8-K filing and company release show, lifting its treasury to 850,364 BTC acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of $75,456. That average cost now sits above the spot bitcoin price, leaving the stack underwater on paper even after the firm added 811 bitcoin the prior week. Strategy’s public ledger still ranks it as the largest corporate bitcoin holder, with the stack equal to roughly 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. MSTR roughly doubled during the third quarter itself. The June 30 13F valued Amundi’s then-smaller stake at an implied $86.93 a share, against the $153.09 Sept. 30 close, so the dollar value of the position rose faster than the share count. Since then the stock has tracked bitcoin’s slide into the mid-$70,000s, wiping out a large share of that mark-to-market gain for anyone still holding the Sept. 30 position. The timing matters because Strategy funds most of its bitcoin buys by selling new MSTR common under an at-the-market program. A weaker share price raises more dilution for every coin purchased, which is the feedback loop that has defined the stock’s moves this year. Banks loaded bitcoin proxies in the same quarter Amundi was not the only large European name adding bitcoin exposure on the quarter. Elizabeth Warren plans to crack down on prediction markets once she takes the Senate Banking Committee gavel in January, with a banking aide telling Punchbowl News that Warren would seek to stop the sector’s “Wild West-style lack of oversight.” The Massachusetts Democrat is poised to chair the panel after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress last week, putting her in charge of a portfolio that covers banking, housing, the Federal Reserve and cryptocurrency. Punchbowl published the aide’s rundown of her agenda on Monday. Warren intends to use the committee’s investigative powers for oversight of prediction markets and election betting platforms, aimed at insider trading and platform manipulation — the same fight she opened before the midterms. That earlier push was bipartisan. On Oct. 28, Warren and Sen. John Curtis, R-Utah, wrote to Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour and Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan asking how the companies stop candidates, campaign staff and others with material nonpublic information from trading election contracts. What Warren and Curtis asked Kalshi and Polymarket “We are particularly troubled by election-related event contracts,” the senators wrote . “Event contracts tied to elections receive prominent coverage and are treated by some observers as indicators of political momentum. There are also documented cases of candidates betting on their own races, which undermines the overall integrity of the American electoral process.” The letter cited candidates who traded on their own contests on Kalshi, including a February 2026 California gubernatorial race, and pointed to research alleging wash trading and volume manipulation on Polymarket. It also referenced an NPR investigation of campaign insiders who said they traded ahead of polling releases. “The identification of isolated instances of improper trading does not demonstrate that these markets are adequately protected,” Warren and Curtis wrote . “Instead, it raises serious questions about how much similar activity may be going undetected.” They asked for written answers by Election Day, Nov. 3. Kalshi’s head of enforcement, Robert DeNault, told Business Insider that the company “proactively blocks candidates and campaign staff from trading to protect market integrity.” Polymarket did not respond to that request for comment. entertainment.title: 5 New Albums to Listen to This Week: Skepta, Phyno, Ty Bello & More
entertainment.description: Skepta holding the official clear vinyl edition of his sixth studio album, The Fork and Knife. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. The project closes with “ Belly ”, an eight-minute masterclass featuring Boy Better Know members Jme and Frisco . ﻿ Phyno: Let That Sink In Arriving nearly 10 years after his groundbreaking sophomore record The Playmaker, Phyno’s 15-track sixth solo album, Let That Sink In (LTSI), showcases his timeless command of indigenous rap. Across the record,the Enugu-born star blends soul, R&B, and traditional Nigerian sounds to explore faith, resilience, and personal evolution. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. I started at the very bottom, as a sales development representative: the person who makes the first call, sends the message and follows up when nobody replies. Today, I manage a sales team. Somewhere between then and now, I stopped seeing real estate as a business of land and buildings. I started seeing it as a mirror. Put a property in front of a Nigerian, and you will learn, very quickly, how they think about money. Here is some of what that mirror has shown me: A prospect once told me, with complete confidence, “I have my money ready for the land.” We fixed an inspection. We walked the site together under the afternoon sun, red earth on our shoes. Then, standing on the plot, the prospect asked if they could pay next year. I was not angry. I understood. Saying “I am ready” feels good. Being ready is different. It means you have decided what the money is for, and you are willing to let it go. I have seen versions of that moment many times. The client who books an inspection for 2 pm and is still not there at 4 pm. The person who asks for options, receives ten properties that match exactly what they requested, and replies, “Do you have something else?” The buyer who is ready until it is time to decide, and then needs three more months to think. The one who disappeared after asking for a price came back after the price went up, and asked for the old price. For a long time, these moments frustrated me. The Wolverines’ head coach made the decision to fire offensive coordinator Jason Beck after an unsatisfactory run of performances, but he still needs to win games to keep his own job secure. Ahead of the game against the Oregon Ducks, who are themselves turning a corner after some tough results, Whittingham shifted attention to Oregon’s massive recruiting budget, highlighting the difference between the two sides. “He really does a great job recruiting and it doesn’t hurt that you have $50+ million dollars at your disposal to, in essence outbid everybody. Not everybody, but a lot of people. But that’s not his fault,” Whittingham said about head coach Dan Lanning to reporters, via Inside Michigan . He further said that he meant it as a credit to the program and its desire to focus on young athletes in the NIL era. “That’s a credit. I mean, that’s a credit to their program and their dedication and desire to win and the support they have. NIL is the name of the game in recruiting these days. It’s shifted so much,” he went on. Kyle Whittingham Explained Why He Fired Jason Beck After a tough defeat to Michigan State, offensive coordinator Jason Beck received his marching orders from Kyle Whittingham, and he addressed the decision to media personnel. “Well, watching the film really was the deciding factor, and I had the intention of waiting until after the season, as I mentioned,” Whittingham said to reporters, as reported by Wolverines Wire . The West Africans face Somalia in back-to-back fixtures over the next week, having lost their first two games in Group C against Ivory Coast and The Gambia last month. Those defeats resulted in the departure of Carlos Queiroz, whose brief period in the hot seat was characterised by uncertainty. The Portuguese's exit means Swede Bjorkegren, who has been in charge of the Black Queens since January 2025, has now been asked to lead the men's team against Somalia. "When you have inconsistency in the amount of time when a manager is staying, it's never good," Hughton told BBC Sport Africa. "You want that consistency in the players [and] the players want that consistency in what they see in the manager." Queiroz, who had two spells as Sir Alex Ferguson's assistant at Manchester United, was initially appointed in April and led Ghana to the last 32 of the Fifa World Cup, holding England to a goalless draw in the group stage, before announcing his own departure shortly after the team were eliminated 1-0 by Colombia in the last 32. However, the 73-year-old was reappointed in early September, with the Ghana Football Association (GFA) praising his "extensive international experience" gained during time in charge of South Africa, Egypt, Portugal, Iran, Colombia, Qatar and Oman. But Queiroz's return lasted less than a month following a 2-0 defeat by the Ivorians in Bouake and a 4-2 humbling against the Gambians in front of home fans in Accra. "What I saw in the World Cup is that they represented the country very well, particularly the England game," said Hughton. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division’s basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don’t like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday’s game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that’s just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don’t do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

sports.title: FIA boss looks to ‘end age limits’ for office holders – six months after ditching term limits
sports.description: Mohammed Ben Sulayem is reportedly looking to end age limits for FIA office holders – just six months after the FIA president ditched term limits for those in leadership posts. Emirati executive Ben Sulayem, 64, has been FIA president since December 2021 and was re-elected last year after other candidates were prevented from standing, due to quirks in the FIA statutes which meant the only prospective vice-president in one region was already aligned with Ben Sulayem. Currently, FIA statutes rule out anyone over the age of 75 from standing for a presidential term. This rule was implemented in 2024 to “modernise the governance of the FIA and ensure that candidates for the presidency are more aligned with current leadership practices.” Yet just six months after Ben Sulayem ended term limits for those in leadership posts, the BBC reports that Ben Sulayem wants to discontinue the age-limit rule and put forward a proposal detailing as such to the FIA’s General Assembly in Shanghai next month. An FIA spokesperson told The Independent: “An age limit excludes candidates solely on the basis of their date of birth, regardless of their experience, expertise, or ability to contribute. Ultimately, the competent FIA bodies will retain full authority to elect the officeholders they deem appropriate.” “The proposal to remove age limits for FIA officeholders is one of the proposed amendments to the FIA Statutes to be put to the General Assembly in Shanghai in December. It was approved by the World Councils for submission in line with the process set out in the FIA Statutes, and will only take effect if the General Assembly votes in favour.” Ben Sulayem had originally introduced an upper age limit of 70 in 2023, in a move widely seen to prevent Motorsport UK boss David Richards from running. Ben Sulayem, who is a regular in parc ferme and on the podium after F1 races, has overseen controversial moments in his near-five years in charge. Ben Sulayem has clashed with Max Verstappen in the past (Getty) His first term saw Ben Sulayem clash with Lewis Hamilton over the Brit’s desire to wear jewellery in the cockpit, while he also angered drivers, including four-time world champion Max Verstappen, for issuing fines for swearing. Last April, Robert Reid resigned as deputy president for sport, accusing the governing body of a "breakdown in governance standards." And presidential candidates such as Tim Mayer and Laura Villars were unhappy after they could not oppose him in last year’s presidential elections. FIA rules dictate a vice-president candidate must be nominated from each of its six global regions; Bernie Ecclestone’s wife, Fabiana, the sole South American candidate, supported Ben Sulayem. Meanwhile, Ben Sulayem has also voiced his support for end-of-season races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi to go ahead. A final call is expected on Tuesday.

sports.title: Jazz Chisholm Jr. Faces Short Deal Path Like Bo Bichette
sports.description: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Jazz Chisholm Jr. is not going to get the same big money that Bo Bichette secured in free agency last year. Bichette left the Toronto Blue Jays for a three-year, $126 million pact with the New York Mets. The Bichette pact averages out to $42 million per year. The key to that massive contract was the opt-out clauses Bichette added after each season. He could have hit the open market this winter but chose to stay, and he holds that same power again next year. Chisholm now faces a similar path to get his value right, though the market looks much tougher for him. A Tough Market for a Talented Player USA Today’s Bob Nightengale wrote a piece on Monday about ten free agents who will draw close attention soon. He looked specifically at Chisholm’s situation and the idea of using an opt-out clause. Nightengale wrote that “He could be in for a rude awakening in the free agent market with executives openly wondering if anyone would give him more than a two-year contract.” The Yankees did not make a qualifying offer to Chisholm, so he is now a free agent. This means teams can sign him without paying a draft pick to New York, but it also signals the team is ready to move on if the price is too high. Despite the rough talk from front offices, Chisholm brings real skills to the table. He is a year removed from a 30/30 season where he hit 30 home runs and stole 30 bases. In 2026, he set a career high with 41 stolen bases in 50 attempts. That speed was a bright spot even if his overall hitting numbers were down. He has played second base since the trade from the Marlins and has graded out well there based on defensive metrics. He also has experience playing center field. His talent is undeniable, but teams worry about his consistency over a long term. Experts Predict a Reset Strategy Nightengale noted that “No one can debate his talent. He may need an opt-out on any multi-year proposal so he can hit market again and re-establish himself.” This strategy mirrors what Bichette did. If Chisholm signs for two years, he can prove he is healthy and hitting, then test the market again for a bigger deal. Various outlets have different guesses on what he might get. According to reports, Chisholm’s potential deals are either 3 years/$110 million or 7 years/$185 million. sports.title: Former Royals catcher and manager Bob Boone dies at age 78
sports.description: BOSTON, MA - MAY 22: Bob Boone #8 of the Kansas City Royals takes a swing during a baseball game against the Boston Red Sox on May 22, 1989 at Fenway Park in Boston, Massachusetts. (Photo by Mitchell Layton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bob Boone, a four-time All-Star catcher who spent two seasons as a player with the Kansas City Royals before managing the club for parts of three seasons, has died at the age of 78, according to a social media post from his family . The son of All-Star infielder Ray Boone, and the father of All-Star infielders Bret and Aaron Boone, the Boones were the first family to have three generations of MLB players. RIP Bob Boone, the great Gold Glove, All Star and World Series champion catcher, who passes away at 78. Condolences to wife Sue and sons Aaron and Bret Boone. What a marvelous man and privilege and honor to know. — Bob Nightengale (@BNightengale) November 10, 2026 Bob Boone was one of the most accomplished defensive catchers of his generation, winning seven Gold Glove Awards over a 19-year playing career. He was originally drafted by the Philadelphia Phillies after a standout career at Stanford. He he finished third in Rookie of the Year voting and was a three-time All-Star with the Phillies. He faced the Royals in the 1980 World Series as a catcher for the Phillies, hitting .412 (7-for-17) in the series for his only championship. He moved onto the Angels in 1982, helping them win the division in their first year, earning MVP votes, and winning a Gold Glove. He was an All-Star the next year, and over seven years in Anaheim, he set the club record for most games behind the plate. He left Anaheim and signed with the Royals in 1989 at the age of 41. He appeared in 131 games and hit .274/.351/.323, winning his seventh Gold Glove and finishing with 2.4 rWAR. After 40 games in 1990, he retired. After the 1994 season was cancelled during the work stoppage, the Royals hired Bob Boone as manager to replace Hal McRae and usher in a new youth movement. Despite trading away stars like David Cone and Brian McRae, the Royals were in the hunt for the new “Wild Card” spot for most of the season, until a poor September caused them to fall under .500 at 70-74. Boone was a very cerebral manager, but would frequently clash with the media. He was criticized for constantly changing the lineup, and for employing “Boonieball,” as then-Kansas City Star columnist Jeffrey Flanagan would call his style of play. Boone finished just 75-86 in 1996, and was fired at the 1997 All-Star break after a 36-46 start, replaced by Tony Muser. Boone would later manage the Cincinnati Reds from 2001-2003, although he never managed them to a winning season. He joined the Washington Nationals front office in 2005 and served the team until he retired in 2021.

But the club has won just one of four games since giving him time to turn things around last month, leaving United one point off the bottom of the table. technology.title: Stanford's century-long AI study admits it's already out of date
technology.description: Twelve years into Stanford's 100-year study of artificial intelligence, the project's third report raises more questions than it answers. The 2026 AI100 Study Panel report acknowledges its limitations in its twelfth takeaway: "This report will be out of date by the time you read it." But it's nonetheless a worthwhile exercise for those who haven't been paying close attention to the development of machine learning over the past few years and for policymakers who may benefit from a review of AI's metastatic growth. "The last five years constitute a watershed moment in the history of AI," said Professor Sheila McIlraith, chair of the AI100 Standing Committee, in a statement. " This report examines what led to the extraordinary capabilities of today's AI systems, and how they are reshaping society. As we look ahead, we anticipate continued increase in AI capabilities alongside transformative advances in science and medicine. "Rapid change will challenge governments and industry to support and safeguard our people, our institutions, and our critical infrastructure. Both the benefits and the risks of AI technologies require the same clear-eyed scrutiny." Established in 2014, the One Hundred Year Study on Artificial Intelligence (AI100) is overseen by a Standing Committee of AI experts and administered by Stanford's Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence (HAI). It's charged with producing reports every five years, the first of which debuted in 2016. The 2026 report's other key points highlight the transformation brought about by increasingly capable machine learning software. It identifies scaling as the engine of AI's advance, but also points to the growing cost and difficulty of obtaining training data as constraints on further progress. The report likens AI's disruptive potential to that of the World Wide Web – without dwelling on the irony that the web itself is among the things being disrupted. It points to creative industries, computer programming, and mathematics as fields once deemed beyond the reach of automation that are now being upended. Science, the report says, is being transformed by AI as it accelerates research timelines and opens up novel challenges. At the same time, the report cautions that "we will need to understand how AI-mediated information environments reshape collective cognition and moral behavior." "Google is aware that an exploit for CVE-2026-125350 exists in the wild," the company said, offering little else about the attacks. The vulnerability was reported anonymously on November 6 and involves a memory management error that occurs when software continues using a pointer to memory that has already been freed. Such bugs can potentially allow attackers to corrupt memory and execute malicious code, although Google hasn't disclosed how this particular flaw is being exploited. Google is keeping further technical details under wraps until enough users have installed the fix, a familiar approach intended to stop other attackers from getting their hands on a working exploit. The patch arrives in Chrome 157.0.8103.50/.51 for Windows and macOS, and 157.0.8103.50 for Linux. The update also addresses eight other security vulnerabilities, including high-severity flaws affecting WebGL, FileSystem, GPU, Compositing, and the V8 JavaScript engine. The release fixes another use-after-free bug in Chrome's XML component, CVE-2026-125346, which was reported by Arni Hardarson of Neonix Security in October, though Google hasn't indicated that this second vulnerability is being exploited. The latest discovery adds to what's becoming a rather long list of Chrome zero-days this year. By June, Google had already patched five actively exploited Chrome zero-days , including flaws in its V8 JavaScript engine, Skia graphics library, and WebGPU implementation. The list has only grown since then, with two more V8 bugs fixed in September and the latest XML vulnerability bringing the total to eight. That puts 2026 level with 2025, when Google also fixed eight Chrome zero-days exploited in the wild. Whether the browser maker can make it through the remaining weeks of the year without adding another to the pile is anyone's guess. Google says the latest update will roll out over the coming days and weeks, but users can check manually by heading to Chrome's Settings menu and selecting About Chrome. With attackers already making use of the vulnerability, it's probably worth doing that sooner rather than waiting for Chrome to get around to it. ®

technology.title: Ransomware threat blares from Vanderbilt University computers during cyberattack
technology.description: Classes at Vanderbilt University are proceeding as scheduled today, although access to most university systems remains restricted following a cyberattack claimed by ransomware group BYOD. Vanderbilt announced on Monday morning that it was dealing with "an active cybersecurity incident," and that the fallout may affect university devices, systems, and cloud-based services. The Nashville-based university initially told students and staff to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. It warned them to watch for unexpected prompts, altered files or permissions, unfamiliar applications, and unsolicited authentication requests. Campus computers reportedly began playing an audio threat attributed to BYOD. Student newspaper The Vanderbilt Hustler cited posts on campus social network Fizz showing the message. "You have been compromised by BYOD," the recording said. "We suggest you reach out to us as soon as possible. Instructions have been placed on your desktop. Failure to communicate will result in this estate being brought to the ground completely. Make the right choice or rot with the wrong one." By Monday evening, Vanderbilt had restored access to campus Wi-Fi, but warned that access to most systems remains restricted. "We know this has disrupted important work and caused frustration across the university," it said . "Vanderbilt Information Technology is working with government agencies and other partners to manage this situation." Students were told to attend classes as scheduled on Tuesday and contact instructors about flexibility on coursework deadlines. Staff were instructed to report to work normally. Vanderbilt's Athletics department said that its ticketing system was unavailable, and that students were unable to claim tickets for the college's football game against Alabama on Saturday. BYOD claimed responsibility for the attack on Vanderbilt on Monday, along with extensive data theft. "If you could not tell already, your databases are locked [and] we have your entire estate and research data," it said via its leak site. "Over 1 million SSNs, full names, email addresses, phone numbers, student and employee records, full takeover of your DC, whatever was on your network, we possess." Vanderbilt has not confirmed BYOD's claims about the extent of its access or the data allegedly stolen. BYOD may be a familiar name to some. The group previously claimed attacks on the University of New Mexico and Trump Mobile's customer database . BYOD also claimed responsibility on Monday for an attack on Texas Health and Human Services. The agency has not publicly confirmed an incident and did not immediately respond to our questions. ®
